[Example project. The chart is built with pandas and Plotly when the site renders. The figures need checking against the House of Commons Library before this goes live.]{.placeholder}

```{python}
#| echo: false
import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go
import plotly.io as pio

# Embed plotly.js in the page so the chart works without a third-party CDN
pio.renderers.default = "notebook"

df = pd.read_csv("../../data/turnout.csv")
green = "#22694D"

fig = go.Figure(go.Scatter(
    x=df.year, y=df.turnout_pct,
    mode="lines+markers",
    line=dict(color=green, width=2),
    marker=dict(size=6, color=green),
    customdata=df.election,
    hovertemplate="%{customdata}: %{y:.1f}%<extra></extra>",
))
fig.update_layout(
    template="simple_white",
    height=380,
    margin=dict(l=10, r=10, t=10, b=10),
    font=dict(family="Geist, sans-serif", size=13, color="#1D2420"),
    plot_bgcolor="#F7F8F6", paper_bgcolor="#F7F8F6",
    yaxis=dict(title="Turnout (%)", range=[55, 88], gridcolor="#D8E0DB", showgrid=True),
    xaxis=dict(title=None, tickvals=[1945, 1955, 1964, 1974, 1983, 1992, 2001, 2010, 2019]),
)
fig.add_annotation(x=1950, y=83.9, text="1950: post-war high", showarrow=False, yshift=14, font=dict(size=12, color="#59635D"))
fig.add_annotation(x=2001, y=59.4, text="2001: lowest since 1918", showarrow=False, yshift=-16, font=dict(size=12, color="#59635D"))
fig.show(config={"displayModeBar": False})
```

## About the data

Turnout is the number of valid votes cast as a percentage of the registered electorate. February and October 1974 are shown as separate elections.
